title: I know, another cozy game. But, I've always wanted to run my own game shop.
author: whatisinaname513
selftext:
I'm probably going about vibecoding all wrong, but I've been working on this project for about a month now. It's been entirely in Claude Code. Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.5.

I did start out with some free itch.io art assets, those have been replaced with code created svg. The entire game is now SVG except for the pixel art for the playable card game which was originally created using PixelLab and then tweaked with Claude Code.

The music is also created with Opus 5.5. I'm not entirely in-love with it yet, but it's getting close to the right feeling. The entire process has been a fun way to learn both about game design and also how to get the results I want while iterating with Claude. 

The gameplay isn't revolutionary, it's an obvious "cozy clone". You take over a game shop and slowly build your life in the town. The minigames are what I enjoy the most and spend the most amount of time in and that's the thing that I think makes it different or special.

Every type of game you sell in your store has a playable version in the game. A Marvel Snap like card game (using the cards from the sets you unlock and sell in the store), a press your luck dice game, a resource/trading strategy board game, a turn based tactical combat miniature game, you run your towns TTRPG campaigns as the DM and a platformer arcade game.

I plan to add more and flesh out the existing ones. I currently have two full card sets in the card game whereas there are 12 sets to unlock, collect and sell in your store. Your character gets better at each game the more you play them which unlocks skill level buffs to give you an advantage. But, your fellow townsfolk get the same advantage gain the more they play, too. Fun rivalries are born over a playthrough as you can host tournaments at your shop and participate in them as well.

You can choose to sell the card packs or rip them and build your personal collection. Buy/sell/trade in used product and always talk to your neighbors, they have hard to find items in their own collections, but you need to go to their house to discover them.

To that end, each neighbor has a branching, unique story to experience that is opened up over-time as your friendship level increases. They each have their own voice/tone and likes and dislikes. If you want to go the romance route, that is built out as well. 

Upgrade your shop and your house, customize both at anytime. And, change the look of your character at anytime, too. Hire a friend to work at the shop for you if you want to go out about town. However, that aspect isn't very fleshed out...and not sure if I will to be honest? The game is about running a local game store, not adventuring about town. All the adventuring happens at the game tables or the local pub on game nights.

Plenty more to do and discover, but those are the highlights. Happy to talk about my process and journey so far. It's setup for running on Windows and Linux as well as mobile devices. The mobile is a tad sketchy but it's getting better. Oh, and I've done at least 90% of this from my phone while at work between actual work tasks. So yeah, probably going about this all wrong but I've been having a blast.

Local Game Shop...

comments.author: West_Satisfaction299
comments.body: There's no such thing as too many cozy games. Anywhere we can follow your progress?

replies.author: whatisinaname513
replies.body: I've got the basic itch.io page setup but it's still private and quite a few version pushes behind. I'll update it and make it public and report back/edit original post when done so people can try it out. Never hurts to get more hands-on feedback!
